permit.exempt_list_quote: When do I need a permit? A permit is required for any new construction, addition, alteration, or repair with an estimated cost of labor and material greater than $7,500 or work that is structural (to include installing, removing, or repairing any wall or partition). Replacement of a window(s) and/or a door(s) is considered structural and will require a permit. Roofing Permit - Required for any repairs or installation of roofing which exceeds 100 square feet of area. Electrical Permit - Required when any new electrical circuits are added, extended or service is changed. Plumbing Permit - Required when any new piping, re-piping, or fixtures are added, including backflow devices. Mechanical Permit - Required when any heating or air conditioning equipment is being extended, relocated or changed out, including ductwork. No permit is required for the installation of window A/C units. Gas Permit - Required for any new gas piping, extending existing gas piping, or the installation or replacement of gas appliances. PLEASE NOTE: Each construction trade requires its own permit.
permit.note: The city publishes no list of exempt work that could be read; its FAQ states the rule the other way round (when a permit is needed). Work at or under $7,500 in labor and material needs no permit unless it is structural, and the FAQ counts 'installing, removing, or repairing any wall or partition' as structural. It does not say whether a toilet partition (a stall panel anchored to floor, wall or ceiling) is a 'partition' in that sense, and toilet partitions or compartments are not named. The Commercial Building Permit page adds only: 'Permits are also required for alterations and changes of occupancies.' The ordinance behind the FAQ (Tallahassee Land Development Code, building chapter, on Municode) was not read (403).
permit.second_quote: Permits are also required for alterations and changes of occupancies. Please keep in mind that alterations and changes of occupancies typically follow a separate process.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Tallahassee job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for North Florida humidity and see the rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Tallahassee state offices, university buildings, schools and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Tallahassee applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on December 31, 2026:** Florida replaces its building rules with a new edition that day. If you apply for a permit around that date, ask Tallahassee Building Inspection which edition applies to your project.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Tallahassee requires a permit for an alteration or repair that costs more than $7,500 in labor and materials, and for any work it treats as structural. The city counts installing, removing or repairing any wall or partition as structural work, and doesn't say whether toilet partitions fall under that. Ask Tallahassee Building Inspection whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with Tallahassee Building Inspection. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Tallahassee Building Inspection sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Tallahassee issues permits to Florida licensed contractors. Before a permit is issued, the contractor files a Florida contractor's license with Tallahassee Building Inspection, with a certificate of liability insurance, workers' compensation insurance or a workers' compensation exemption, all current. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with Tallahassee Building Inspection which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Tallahassee files a Florida license and insurance certificates with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $16.00 an hour for a carpenter on building work in Leon County, with no benefits amount listed.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Tallahassee: 6% state and 1.5% Leon County. The county's 1.5% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices and university buildings:** HDPE or phenolic in busy public and student restrooms, with hardware that stands up to heavy daily use.

- The change to the 9th Edition on December 31, 2026: Florida Building Commission, [Workplan, October 2026](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/commission/FBC_1026/Commission/Workplan_October_2026.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts are the state's in Tallahassee: the Florida Building Commission's [report of local technical amendments to the 8th Edition (2023) Florida Building Code, Plumbing](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/thecode/2026_Code_Development/June_2025-1st_Comment/Local_Amendments/PLUMBING-Detail_Report-LA.docx) lists Broward County, Pinellas County and Miami-Dade County only, and Tallahassee's Codes page shows no local amendment. Checked 2026-11-24.

- When Tallahassee requires a permit: City of Tallahassee Growth Management FAQ, [When do I need a permit?](https://www.talgov.com/growth/gm_faqs/62.aspx), and [Commercial Building Permit](https://www.talgov.com/growth/gm_permits_lues/Commercial_Building_Permit_6). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractors in Tallahassee: City of Tallahassee Growth Management FAQ, [When do I need a contractor?](https://www.talgov.com/growth/gm_faqs/65.aspx), and Building Inspection's [Contractor License Registration & Requirements](https://www.talgov.com/Uploads/Public/Documents/growth/forms/contractors-req.pdf) form (revised June 21, 2022). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Leon County: Florida Department of Revenue, [TIP 26A01-22, Leon County Surtax Rate Update (November 20, 2026)](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/Documents/TIP_26A01-22.pdf), [Form DR-15DSS, Discretionary Sales Surtax Information for Calendar Year 2026](https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/dr15dss_26.pdf) and [Discretionary Sales Surtax](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/discretionary.aspx) for the $5,000 limit. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Leon County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination FL20260233, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/FL20260233/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023 (Tallahassee lists them as effective January 1, 2024) and enforced in Tallahassee without local technical amendments; replaced by the 9th Edition (2026) on December 31, 2026; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions counts as 'installing, removing, or repairing any wall or partition' and so needs a Tallahassee permit at any cost (Building Inspection, 850-891-7001, option 2 then option 1, or permits@talgov.com).

Tallahassee has posted no notice of the 9th Edition (2026) changeover; its pages still show the 8th Edition only. The city dates the 8th Edition from January 1, 2024, a day after the state's December 31, 2023, so ask Building Inspection which day it applies the 9th Edition from and what cut-off it uses for applications already filed.
Update on December 31, 2026: rewrite the 'New rules' bullet, recheck the stall table against the published 9th Edition and Tallahassee's Codes page.

Tallahassee's code on Municode could not be opened: read the building chapter of the Land Development Code once in a browser to confirm the $7,500 permit threshold as the ordinance words it, that there is no local technical amendment, and that there is no city restroom-sign rule.
The federal carpenter rate for Leon County ($16.00, no fringe) comes from a 2014 survey and is below the local median of $22.53; it is what the determination lists.
Sales tax: 7.5% confirmed for 2027 by TIP 26A01-22; read the 2027 Form DR-15DSS when the Department posts it.
Properties outside the city limits are permitted by Leon County Development Services (850-606-1300), not the city; the page speaks for the city only.
The Department of Revenue doesn't say whether toilet partitions count as a building fixture or as goods, which decides how an installed job is taxed (same open question as Miami and Tampa).
